title: Objectwise derived evaluation detects comparison direct-image vanishing
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and $\Lambda$ a discrete associative unital ring, not necessarily commutative [def-pc-scheme]. Use the small étale and pro-étale sites in a common larger universe in which they are small [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use sheaves of left modules over the associated constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $
u_X:X_{\mathrm{proét}}	o X_{\mathrm{ét}}$ be the comparison geometric morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]; its module direct image $
u_{X,*}$ is restriction to the étale objects with their induced scalar actions. Let $M$ be any such module sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ and $q>0$ an integer. For each étale $W	o X$, let $\Gamma_{\mathrm{proét},W}$ be evaluation $N\mapsto N(W)$ to abelian groups. Right derived functors here are computed by injective resolutions in the respective module categories [def-sp-left-exact-additive, def-sp-injective-resolutions]. If
$$ R^q\Gamma_{\mathrm{proét},W}(M)=0\quad	ext{for every étale }W	o X, $$
then $R^q
u_{X,*}M=0$ as a module sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$. No assumption that $M$ is an inverse image or injective is made.

source.place: Tag 099V (lemma-relative-comparison), first paragraph: resolution-level objectwise vanishing argument, for arbitrary left-module coefficients; sites-modules.tex Tag 03DA (lemma-abelian).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] to the small pro-étale site and its constant ring sheaf $\Lambda_{X_{\mathrm{proét}}}$. Its left-module category is Grothendieck abelian, with no commutativity hypothesis, so [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] gives enough injectives. Construct a resolution $M\to I^\bullet$ as follows: embed $M$ into an injective $I^0$; embed $I^0/M$ into an injective $I^1$ and define $d^0$ by the quotient followed by this embedding. Recursively embed $\operatorname{coker}(d^{n-1})$ into an injective $I^{n+1}$ and let $d^n$ be the quotient followed by that embedding. The kernel of $d^n$ is the image of $d^{n-1}$, so this is an injective resolution concentrated in nonnegative degrees.

source.place: Tag 079Q (remark-existence-D), with derived.tex Tag 013K (lemma-injective-resolutions-exist), proof of (1)

proof.text: Put $J^\bullet=\nu_{X,*}I^\bullet$. By the injective-resolution definition [def-sp-left-exact-additive], $R^q\nu_{X,*}M=\mathcal H^q(J^\bullet)$, and the same resolution computes $R^q\Gamma_{\mathrm{proét},W}(M)=H^q(I^\bullet(W))$ for each étale $W\to X$. Direct image in the statement is restriction, including on module morphisms; hence $J^n(W)=I^n(W)$ and the differentials agree. Thus the hypothesis says exactly $H^q(J^\bullet(W))=0$ as an abelian group for every such $W$.

source.place: Tag 099V (lemma-relative-comparison), first paragraph; injective-resolution interpretation expanded from the definition

proof.text: In the étale module category let $Z=\ker(d^q:J^q\to J^{q+1})$. Kernels of module sheaves are sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so $Z(W)=\ker(d^q(W))$. Since $d^q d^{q-1}=0$, the previous differential factors as $J^{q-1}\xrightarrow{p}Z\hookrightarrow J^q$. The equality $H^q(J^\bullet(W))=0$ from Step 2 means that every $z\in Z(W)$ equals $d^{q-1}(W)(y)$ for some $y\in J^{q-1}(W)$; consequently $p(W)$ is surjective for every étale $W$. Here $q>0$ ensures that the preceding degree is in the chosen resolution.

source.place: Tag 03DA (lemma-abelian) and preceding construction of kernels; cycle-boundary calculation for the complex in Tag 099V

proof.text: The map $p$ is an epimorphism of module sheaves: if $a,b:Z\to N$ satisfy $a p=b p$, for every $W$ and $z\in Z(W)$ choose $y$ with $p(W)(y)=z$; then $a(W)(z)=a(W)(p(W)(y))=b(W)(p(W)(y))=b(W)(z)$. Equality at every object is equality of sheaf morphisms. Therefore $\operatorname{coker}(p)=0$. The cohomology object $\mathcal H^q(J^\bullet)$ is precisely this cokernel of the preceding differential with codomain restricted to its cycle object $Z$. Step 2 now gives $R^q\nu_{X,*}M=0$.

source.place: Tag 03DA (lemma-abelian); explicit epimorphism and cohomology-cokernel argument

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q24-46e99f3ce (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the delivered item in full, its eight stmt_deps and four proof_deps statements, and the parent lem-pe-comparison-injective-left-modules-acyclic, whose Step 4 hypothesis matches this item exactly. The statement is true for an arbitrary associative ring Λ and arbitrary M; I checked Λ=0, X empty, M_2(F_p), and that no step assumes a module-injective is abelian-injective. Step 1: the Grothendieck lemma and enough injectives give an injective resolution, and the iterative cokernel construction is correct. Step 2: def-sp-left-exact-additive is a Mathlib-matched definition that includes independence of the resolution. Evaluation and ν_* preserve kernels because module kernels are sectionwise, and étale W is an object of X_proét, so J^n(W)=I^n(W). Advisory: left exactness of ν_* is argued only in the report, but the statement fixes this computation. Step 3: the sectionwise kernel clause gives that p(W) is surjective, and q>0 is used correctly. Step 4: a sectionwise surjection is an epimorphism of sheaves, and H^q=coker(J^{q-1}→Z)=0. This is valid and simpler than the 03F3 sheafification route because the hypothesis holds for every étale W. There is no duplicate: det-pe-injective-acyclicity-reduction is for commutative Λ and affine W, and the other candidates are for scheme morphisms or injective inputs. I accept the declared tool_uses: lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck is generic and the parent uses it too, and lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives is a Mathlib leaf. lean.note: Fixed-scalar encoding of sheaves over the associated constant ring sheaf, as in the already recorded parent lem-pe-comparison-injective-left-modules-acyclic. Ring Λ, arbitrary M, and derived abelian evaluation in the module category; no injectivity, finiteness, commutativity or inverse-image assumption. The sites retain object universe u+1 and morphism universe u; modules and coefficients lie in the common larger universe u+1. Comparison direct image is the recorded canonical restriction functor, not an arbitrary map.
